annotation.title_clean: The Civil Aviation (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023
annotation.title_en: The Civil Aviation (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) (Amendment) Regulations, 2023
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United Republic of Tanzania, Minister for Works and Transport
annotation.venue: Gazette of the United Republic of Tanzania No. 19 Vol. 104, Supplement No. 19 (GN No. 365)
named_instruments_referenced: Civil Aviation (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) Regulations, 2018
annotation.summary_en: This is Tanzania's Government Notice 365 of 2023. It amends the 2018 Civil Aviation (Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems) Regulations, which are made under the Civil Aviation Act. It adds definitions, changes the scope of application and the registration marks (from 9XR- to 5H-), and requires special authorisation and detect equipment for drone flights beyond or extended beyond visual line of sight. Operating more than one drone at once needs the Authority's approval.
key_provisions_or_claims: The rules apply to people who operate or maintain RPAS registered in Tanzania.
Flights beyond visual line of sight (BVLoS) or extended beyond visual line of sight (EBVLoS) need special authorisation from the Authority and a detector on board.
No one may operate more than one RPAS at the same time without the Authority's approval.
RPAS registration marks change from 9XR- to 5H-.
The Authority may require additional documents in applications.
